name: Onasemnogene abeparvovec
route_note: Single one-time intravenous infusion dosed by weight in young children; intrathecal formulation for older patients.
originator: Nationwide Children's Hospital (Jerry Mendell, Brian Kaspar) and AveXis

discovery.by: Brian Kaspar and Jerry Mendell, Nationwide Children's Hospital, Columbus, Ohio
discovery.note: Uses a self-complementary AAV9 vector able to cross the blood–brain barrier to deliver a functional SMN1 gene to motor neurons. Year of the first report of the scAAV9-SMN vector rescuing SMA mice (Foust et al., Nat Biotechnol 2010).

tagline: One-time gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, once the world's costliest drug
summary: Onasemnogene abeparvovec is a one-time gene therapy that delivers a working copy of the SMN1 gene using an adeno-associated virus serotype 9 vector. Approved in 2019 for young children with spinal muscular atrophy, its $2.1 million price made it the most expensive drug at the time.
mechanism: The vector carries a human SMN1 transgene under a constitutive promoter. After intravenous infusion, AAV9 crosses the blood–brain barrier and transduces motor neurons and other cells, where the transgene persists as episomal DNA and produces full-length SMN protein.

Because motor neurons do not divide, expression is expected to be long-lasting. Immune responses to the vector capsid and high vector doses underlie hepatotoxicity, so corticosteroids are given around treatment.
uses: Spinal muscular atrophy with bi-allelic SMN1 mutations in children under 2 years (IV)
Spinal muscular atrophy in patients aged 2 years and older (intrathecal, US)

history.title: START trial
history.detail: Mendell et al. (NEJM) report survival without permanent ventilation in all 15 treated infants with SMA type 1.

history.title: Novartis acquires AveXis
history.detail: Novartis buys AveXis for about $8.7 billion.

history.title: FDA approval and data controversy
history.detail: The FDA approves Zolgensma in May at a list price of $2.125 million; in August it discloses that AveXis manipulated some animal-testing data, though product safety was not judged to be affected.

history.title: EU conditional approval
history.detail: The European Commission grants conditional marketing authorisation.

history.title: Liver failure deaths
history.detail: Novartis reports two deaths from acute liver failure, prompting strengthened monitoring.

history.title: Intrathecal formulation
history.detail: The FDA approves intrathecal onasemnogene abeparvovec (Itvisma) for SMA patients aged 2 years and older.

pk.half_life: vector DNA persists in transduced non-dividing cells; shed in stool and urine for weeks

serious: Acute serious liver injury and acute liver failure
safety.boxed_warning: Serious liver injury and acute liver failure, including fatal cases; assess liver function before and after infusion.

facts: Children must test negative or low for anti-AAV9 antibodies before treatment, because pre-existing antibodies can neutralise the vector.
